title: Beta Reduction of the K Combinator
description: Trace how left-associative application reduces the K combinator (λx.λy.x) A B in two beta steps to select the first argument.

steps.description: Line 1 writes `(λx.λy.x) A B`. Because application is left-associative, the outer redex applies `λx.λy.x` to `A` first, with `B` waiting on the outside as `(((λx.λy.x) A) B)`.
Lines 2-3 perform the first beta reduction: `[x := A] (λy.x)` replaces `x` inside `λy.x` with `A`, leaving the constant function `(λy.A)` applied to `B`.

steps.question: When `(λy.A) B` on line 3 reduces by substituting `B` for `y` inside the body `A`, what happens to `B` and what is the final result?
steps.answer: Because `y` does not appear in the body `A`, `[y := B] A` discards `B` and evaluates to `A`.

steps.description: Lines 4-5 apply `[y := B] A`: since `y` never occurs in `A`, `B` drops out and the expression reaches normal form `A`.
